extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, Congress, trademark practitioners, applicants, and other trademark stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and reporting of U.S. trademark program performance, operations, policy actions, and stakeholder-facing initiatives for FY2024, including pendency, examination quality, IT modernization, fee setting, register protection, TTAB performance, and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: First-action pendency is the average time from when a trademark application is filed until the USPTO issues its first examination action (typically an office action or an approval for publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a key pendency metric with FY 2024 goal of 8.4 months; tracked monthly on the Trademark processing wait times page. The report describes causes of elevated pendency (e.g., filing surges, IT transitions) and highlights that reducing this metric was an explicit USPTO objective in the FY 2024 pendency reduction plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposal pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposal pendency is the average time between the date a trademark application is filed and its final disposition by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be lengthened by suspensions awaiting resolution of related matters (earlier-filed applications, litigation, TTAB proceedings, appeals). FY 2024 actual disposal pendency was 14.1 months against a 14.4-month goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting application volume by classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark application filing volume is measured by the number of classes filed (because examining attorneys review each class separately), not by the number of filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This measurement choice affects workload projections and pendency targets; FY 2024 reported 767,138 new trademark application classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO actions to reduce first-action pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational measures implemented under the pendency reduction plan to shorten time to first action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: increasing IT resources supporting internal TM Exam system and training for efficient searching; shifting the 'exceptional' office action standard from first to final action; offering new incentives for examining attorney performance; hiring additional examining attorneys and optimizing Trademark Academy training; directing anti-scam and bad faith review to the Register Protection Office; working with unions on additional trademark professional assistance for pre-registration review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges affecting pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors recognized as slowing pendency improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated challenges include increased fraud monitoring; lengthy custom identifications when applicants draft their own identifications rather than using the Trademark ID Manual; time and resource demands of transitioning to multiple new IT systems after TRAM retirement; and unplanned outages (e.g., CrowdStrike outage) that halt operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible response periods (office action response periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation and scope of flexible office action response periods under the Trademark Modernization Act of 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-registration office actions: shortened response time from six months to three months with an option for one three-month extension for a fee (implemented Dec 2022). USPTO considered but did not implement the same change for post-registration office actions in FY 2024; TPAC supports maintaining current post-registration deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-registration pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time between filing post-registration maintenance documents and USPTO review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY 2024 goals were 90 days for affidavits of use/incontestability, renewals, and amendments/corrections; FY 2024 actuals were 191 days (affidavits), 69 days (renewals), and 158 days (amendments). Causes include staff transition to new IT systems; USPTO hired additional post-registration specialists to address backlog.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time between when an appeal, contested motion, or trial record is ready for decision and when the decision issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTAB FY 2024 goals: Final decisions — Appeals (12 weeks or less), Contested motions — Trials (12 weeks or less), Final decisions — Trials (15 weeks or less). FY 2024 actuals exceeded goal for some categories (e.g., appeals 15.9 weeks). TTAB pendency reporting excludes cases involving precedential orders or anomalous histories. Strategies to reduce pendency include adding judges, Final Pretrial Conference pilot, efficient decision writing, and improved data analysis (including hiring a data analyst).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination quality — First action compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: First action compliance assesses whether the USPTO made the right decision when initially examining the trademark application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracked as a performance measure; FY 2024 target 95.5% and actual 96.0%. The report notes redefinition of standards (moving 'exceptional' standard to final action) to increase efficiency without altering decision standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination quality — Final action compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Final action compliance examines whether the USPTO made the right decision at the examining attorney's final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracked as a performance measure; FY 2024 target 97.0% and actual 98.7%. The 'exceptional' office action standard was moved to final action to require full records only where final refusals are issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Pretrial Conference pilot (TTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot program to require final pretrial conferences in selected trial cases likely to benefit from judicial guidance before trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals: save time and resources, foster effective and efficient presentation of evidence. Cases are selected upon recommendation by administrative trademark judges or interlocutory attorneys and reviewed by a planning team; the pilot includes orientation and the Final Pretrial Conference. Results to date show settlements, narrowed trial scope, or accelerated resolutions in some selected matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case citation pilot (TTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of how TTAB decisions are cited in opinions and orders and evaluation of options for a comprehensive decision repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivated by loss of access to the USPQ reporter; options include private publishers, expanding TTAB tools (TTAB Reading Room, TTABVue), or new comprehensive database. Inputs to be evaluated on comprehensiveness, reliability, accessibility, and cost. Current practice under TBMP §101.3 allows citation to any reliable source.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT modernization and TRAM retirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Retirement of the TRAM mainframe and migration of processes, data, and system functions to cloud and new platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success metrics include completion of migration (retired May 31, 2024), replacement of ~1,500 processes, projected $10 million future savings, enabling further IT investments, increased security and stability, and support for modernization (new search system, Trademark Center, TM Exam). Acknowledges training needs and short-term productivity impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: New trademark search system
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement of TESS with a modern trademark search system offering updated interface and search functionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Launched Dec 1, 2023; aims to provide a modern search experience (reported >1 million searches/week), supported by comprehensive help documentation and training tailored to user knowledge levels. TPAC commends soliciting and incorporating customer feedback through outreach and social listening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Center implementation (filing platform modernization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Development and phased rollout of Trademark Center to replace TEAS as the central hub for trademark filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademark Center tested with diverse customers; planned to support all initial applications by calendar year 2025. During transition TEAS will operate concurrently. Expected benefits: enhanced filing experience, promote complete/focused goods & services descriptions to improve examination efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB Center (TTAB e-filing modernization)
rubrics_metrics.description: New electronic filing system for TTAB proceedings to replace ESTTA, with enhanced security and data capture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features: USPTO.gov account requirement and two-factor authentication to reduce fraudulent filings; only requester may file a Notice of Opposition for a matter; improved data collection/analysis capabilities to replace manual assembly of ESTTA data. Phased beta releases for Notice of Opposition and Petition to Cancel tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial framework and operating reserve management
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and cash management principles for a fee-funded USPTO including maintaining an operating reserve to manage revenue variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO must plan budgets long in advance; uses operating reserve to smooth demand volatility. FY 2024 trademark operating reserve was $161.5 million (above minimum target $135 million). The report uses these financial principles to justify fee adjustments and longer-term planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee setting to recover anticipated aggregate costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory obligation for the USPTO to set fees at levels that will recover anticipated aggregate costs, implemented through notice-and-comment rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPAC evaluated proposed fee changes, found proposal appropriate with recommended clarifications. NPRM published Mar 26, 2024; public comment period followed. USPTO anticipates final rule Q1 FY 2025 and fee adjustments effective Jan 2025 (some later). Projected revenue increases used to close multi-year revenue gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure fee setting authority (policy stability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that Congress provide permanent fee setting authority to avoid planning uncertainty and preserve USPTO's fiscal management capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: AIA fee setting authority was time-limited and set to expire in 2026; TPAC urges Congressional action to make authority permanent to support long-term planning and statutory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding fee revenue diversion / sequestration protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that USPTO user fees should support USPTO operations and not be subject to sequestration or diversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPAC argues sequestration is unjustified for USPTO because it is fee-funded and does not contribute to federal deficit; sequestration could divert up to ~9% of user fees mid-year with disproportionate impacts. Notes legal exception language and administrative determinations to date; urges protection from sequestration to preserve planned investments (e.g., pendency reduction, IT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-registration audits (selection and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Random audits of registrations to preserve the accuracy and integrity of the trademark register by confirming use in commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection criteria: registrations with timely Section 8 or 71 filings and either at least one class with four or more goods/services or two classes with two or more goods/services. Since 2017, the USPTO audited >10,000 registrations annually (FY 2024: 4,723 audits). Purpose: promote reliable IP rights and maintain register integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte non-use cancellation proceedings (expungement and reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative proceedings to cancel some or all goods/services in a registration based on lack of use in commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expungement: canceling goods/services because registrant never used the mark in commerce for those goods/services. Reexamination: canceling goods/services in a use-based registration because the mark was not in use on or before the required date. Either the public or the Under Secretary may initiate petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative sanctions program and anti-scam measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Program and enforcement tools to address solicitation and impersonation scams and other fraudulent filings affecting trademark practice and USPTO systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified scam types include sponsorship scams, filing firm scams, fake correspondence, false association scams, and government impersonation. Responses include requiring ID verification for sponsored USPTO accounts, public awareness campaigns, warnings in filing platforms and receipts, maintaining administrative sanctions and orders, increased reporting to FTC/FBI, and collaboration with search engines to remove misleading ads. Possible sanctions: disregard affected submissions, terminate proceedings (including terminating applications), preclude filing documents, deactivate USPTO.gov accounts, and refer to Office of Enrollment and Discipline. Program metrics: over 329 sanction orders, termination of >20,196 invalid filings, sanctioning >3,298 invalid registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-counterfeiting outreach effectiveness (Go for Real campaign)
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational outreach metrics and goals aimed at reducing counterfeit product use, especially among youth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campaign channels include PSAs, videos, interactive content, handouts, posters, social media, radio, and school programs. Reported outcomes: 56% of teens who recalled the campaign engaged with materials; 67% ensure products are not fake after exposure; 62% know how to spot a fake (up from 39%); campaign >2 billion impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Public Engagement and targeted outreach programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidation of outreach programs into OPE to increase participation in the innovation ecosystem and improve IP literacy and access for underrepresented communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPE components: Council of Inclusive Innovation, Regional Outreach Offices, Strategic Engagement Office, Community Engagement Office. Programs include veterans, military teachers, rural and tribal outreach, IP champions, and expanded pro bono trademark clinic certification; emphasizes evidence-based strategies and targeted deployment of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible exploration and use of AI in trademark operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that USPTO should explore AI to augment capabilities while maintaining high-quality human trademark review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential AI uses mentioned: detecting fraudulent specimens, streamlining goods and services descriptions, assisting internal search capabilities. Emphasizes nuanced human analysis remains necessary and AI should be applied in targeted, responsible ways to increase efficiency without compromising quality.
